A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 22-page versions of the same PARS study, including Appendices A-H. Text and rendered-page comparisons support assessment of all sections, equations, figures, and tables without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original PARS benchmark evaluations, online fine-tuning results, toy regression experiments, and ablations, including Tables 2-5 and Appendices A, D, G, and H.

after.justification: v2 retains the original PARS experiments, benchmark results, ablations, and computational measurements reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1-4.3 retain identical reward scaling with layer normalization, infeasible-action penalties, sampling procedures, and critic ensembles. The TD3+BC-based algorithm and Section 6.5 application to IQL are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 28 D4RL datasets across AntMaze, Adroit, and MuJoCo, including AntMaze Ultra. The toy regression scenarios in Section 4 and Appendix D are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the offline, online fine-tuning, and goal-conditioned comparisons in Tables 2-4 and the appendix comparisons in Tables 6-7. Figure 19 retains the same computational-cost baselines.

E3.justification: The normalized-score evaluations, 300k-sample online fine-tuning budget, model configurations, hyperparameter settings, and data-mixing procedures are unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix F. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Section 6.4 and Appendices D and G retain the same component ablations, reward-scaling and dormant-neuron analyses, infeasible-action distance tests, and sensitivity studies for penalty weights, critic counts, and activation functions.

E5.justification: Five-seed averaging and standard-deviation reporting remain identical, including table uncertainties, ablation error bars, and shaded learning curves in Appendix A. No run-count or statistical-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, PARS's AntMaze averages remain 81.6 offline in Table 2 and 95.2 after fine-tuning in Table 3; appendix results and computational measurements are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses, and sampling equations are identical. Appendix C retains the same contraction argument and derivations comparing TD3+BC and IQL critic updates.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about mitigating extrapolation through reward scaling and infeasible-action penalties, PARS's simplicity, and its offline and online fine-tuning performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of the experiments are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same qualifications concerning positive target Q-values and dependence on critic ensembles.

D1.justification: Appendices E, F, and H retain identical implementation code, hyperparameters, hardware information, and PARS code-access instructions. The JAX bibliography URL update identifies the same cited software and does not establish changed resources or reproducibility procedures.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The Bradbury et al. JAX reference only changes its URL from github.com/google/jax to github.com/jax-ml/jax; it remains the same cited work.

P1.justification: The JAX reference URL is updated, and the first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 11 July 2025 to v2 dated 19 August 2025. All substantive prose, terminology, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, and placements are unchanged. Rendered pages match except for the version/date stamp and JAX URL characters, with no figure, table, or page-layout revision.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves all scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendix material. Updating the JAX bibliographic URL and arXiv stamp produces no meaningful overall quality difference; no substantive deficiency is resolved or introduced.
